messages.subject: Using RHipe
parts:
Hi All,

I am using the following command to read a
x<-rhread('/usr/hadoop/input/salls').
However the R object 'x' appears to be a matrix of 1 column that has
all the information under the same column.

store_no,fiscal_wk,sales,std_sales
101,201045,578556,74.567
102,201034,46587,576.6
103,20217,4356356,67

Is there a better way to the above operation so that i can have a
proper table in place of the above result.
Please let me know.

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Using RHipe
parts:
you need to provide more information.


1. Did you read a text file? It appears you read a sequence file .
if it's the latter, you get what is stored - which is  matrix of 1 column.

2. With a text file, you also get what rows of text which need to be strspliteed and made into columns.

I find it handy to keep  a includeme.R file which has handy functions for RHIPE use.

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Using RHipe
parts:
I don't know of a simple function. I do it with:

data = as.character(unlist(map.values))
data = strsplit(data, ",")
data = do.call("rbind", data)

If there is a header line polluting a csv I check for it after that with something like:

year = data[,1]
header.row = year == "Year"
data = data[!header.row,,drop=FALSE]
if(nrow(data) == 0){
rhcounter("MAP","NO DATA", 1)  # a curious case
return()
}


I think fix up the columns with something like:

colnames(data) = colnames
data = as.data.frame(data,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
data = as.list(data)
integers = c(1:8,12:13,15:16)
suppressWarnings({
data[integers] = lapply(data[integers],as.integer)  #"NA" to NA makes a warning.
})
data = as.data.frame(data)
